cards.expected_note:
Very big house in very good repair.
Very well-furnished - obviously
well-to-do home.
Dining room has doors opening into lounge
Very good garden - fish pond, fernery etc.

Young girl employed in shop.
Saw son (head) - did not see over
house. Not prepared to furnish
information re net profit - appears
prosperous business.
[illegible] fair repair.

No one at home [illegible] 24/9
Very good type of house - in very good repair (modern)
bright, large, airy rooms - well decorated &
well furnished.
Saw wife. [illegible] 25/9/41.

Very good type of house - in v. gd. condition externally
Very nicely decorated & furnished inside.
Rooms bright, clean & airy.
Wife says husband did not want her to give information.
I persuaded her to give me partics. re house & family
but she did not wish to say What husband did or earned.
I think he probably works on Railways at Newport &
may be on office staff as he has once been an office worker
I gathered from her conversation.

Wife interviewed - very co-operative. Son has had pleurisy & unable
to work for past year

The Mother was interviewed. She did not know what the various members of the
family earned. She said the only thing that mattered to her was their money.
The same applied to the boarders. The 1st boarder had been called up and was
going into Camp for the duration of the War. The Son that was Missing had not been
living at home for some time.
The house was in fair order, needed papering inside, they were buying through
the Credit Foncier.
The allotment was about 30 x 80ft.
